extracted.intended_audience: researchers and stakeholders in scholarly publishing (authors, reviewers, editors, institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural features governing how Peer Community In (PCI) communities review, validate, and recommend preprints, and how those recommendations are presented and used. Focuses on openness, transparency, editorial structure, and interoperability with traditional journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be accessible in open archives in accordance with the principle of open access (free access for the author and for the reader).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI provides scientific validation of manuscripts accessible in open archives; recommendations are made for preprints available publicly (examples: arXiv, bioRxiv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed, citable recommendations with DOI
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations of experts are accessible to the reader and citable because they are signed and provided with a digital object identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI makes reviews/recommendations public, signed by recommenders, and issues DOIs so recommendations can be cited like other scholarly outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary recommendation decision
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI differs from other preprint-review platforms by making the binary decision to recommend (or not) a preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The core editorial outcome is a clear recommend / not recommend decision rather than only posting reviews or comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with traditional publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript recommended by a PCI remains free for later publication in most classic scientific journals and PCI recommendations can be integrated into journal editorial processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI is not affected by the Ingelfinger rule; authors often submit PCI-reviewed preprints to journals and some journals accept PCI reviews as part of their editorial assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement-recommendation cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who submit to a PCI benefit from an improvement-recommendation cycle (reviews leading to suggested improvements before recommendation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is iterative: reviews can lead to revisions and subsequent recommendation, helping authors improve manuscripts prior to journal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No publication/subscription fees in editorial model
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial model does not provide financial resources for authors' publication costs, readers' consultation costs, or subscription fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI communities are modestly funded and the system is presented as free for both authors and readers (no APCs or subscription costs borne by the PCI model itself).

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-based editorial structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disciplinary PCI is made up of a management board (~ten recognized experts), several tens or hundreds of associate editors ('recommenders'), and involves external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions and the recommendation process are managed by community-specific boards and recommenders; governance is local to each discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary recommendation allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The same manuscript can be recommended by PCIs from several disciplines, facilitating interdisciplinary recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PCI recommends preprints (rather than publishing them exclusively), a work relevant to multiple fields may receive recommendations from multiple PCI communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation like a classic journal with increased transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Peer Community Journal is presented like a classic scientific journal but PCI provides more transparent and advanced services while remaining free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2021, recommended preprints may be published in the Peer Community Journal, combining journal-like presentation with PCI’s transparent review documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional recognition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Some higher education institutions accept PCI-recommended preprints as equivalent to a publication in a peer-reviewed scientific journal when the preprint is in an open archive and recommended by PCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions that support PCI commit to: consider PCI legitimate for evaluating results; treat PCI-recommended manuscripts like traditional articles; and encourage community members to use PCI practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of PCI communities
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI operates multiple thematic communities (e.g., Ecology, Evolutionary Biology, Genomics, Psychology, Registered Reports) each with their own managing board and remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit to the PCI community corresponding to their sub-field; some communities explicitly handle specific formats like Registered Reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accessibility of reviews vs other platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI provides transparent, signed recommendations (citable) and differs from other preprint-review platforms that may only host reviews without issuing a formal recommend/not recommend decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare with platforms like PREreview and Review Commons: PCI’s distinct feature is the formal binary recommendation combined with signed, citable reviews.
